title: VoteGEO-Bench: Measuring the Impact of Generative Engine Optimization on Electoral Visibility
abstract: arXiv:2610.21330v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for election information, yet little is known about how external web content shapes the political information they present. Generative engine optimization (GEO) rewrites web content to improve its visibility in generated responses. To investigate its potential risks in voting scenarios (VoteGEO), we introduce VoteGEO-Bench, a benchmark covering the 2024 U.S. presidential election and the 2026 Japanese House of Representatives election, combining election-related queries, historical webpages, and voter personas. We first analyze sources cited by generative engines and find that many citations come from lower-cost owned and open-platform sources, while some webpages remain visible across days. translated_title: VoteGEO-Bench：衡量生成式引擎优化对选举可见性的影响
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）日益被用于获取选举信息，但外部网页内容如何塑造其所呈现的政治信息仍鲜为人知。生成式引擎优化（GEO）通过改写网页内容来提升其在生成式回答中的可见性。为探究其在投票场景中的潜在风险，我们提出了VoteGEO-Bench，一个覆盖2024年美国总统大选和2026年日本众议院选举的基准，其中结合了选举相关查询、历史网页和选民画像。我们首先分析了生成式引擎所引用的来源，发现许多引用来自成本较低的自有来源和开放平台来源，而部分网页能够在多天内持续保持可见。随后，我们评估了4大类共11种改写策略，考察了目标指定方式、跨引擎与跨选举的有效性以及选民画像所起的作用。未指定目标的改写（摘要原文在此处截断）……
tldr: 该论文提出VoteGEO-Bench基准，覆盖美日两国选举场景，系统评估了11种生成式引擎优化（GEO）改写策略对LLM生成回答中政治信息可见性的影响，揭示了选举信息可能被低成本来源与改写策略操纵的潜在风险。
